title: Supported realized behavior preserves intended mandatory passage
statement: Supported realized behavior MUST NOT reach a checkpoint while bypassing a checkpoint that dominates it in the Intended BFG.
rationale: Intended dominators encode semantic gates that every meaningful route must traverse. A supported implementation path around such a gate is a behavioral contradiction even when individual functions and architectural dependencies are otherwise valid.
failure_prevented: Protected operations, accepted-only processing, or other meaningful checkpoints being reachable through supported implementation semantics without their required behavioral gate.
applicability: Every opted-in modeled Feature whose Intended BFG contains a dominator relation and whose relevant implementation region has sufficient supported semantic coverage.
evaluation: Fortress compares Intended BFG dominators with exact implementation-event reachability and emits a finding only for an actual supported route that reaches the dominated checkpoint while excluding every anchor of the required dominator.

finding.message: Supported implementation behavior bypasses an Intended BFG dominator.

remediation: Correct implementation control and semantic flow so every route to the reached checkpoint passes the required dominator, or correct inaccurate behavioral intent.
valid_example: Every supported route reaching a protected-operation checkpoint first passes an authentication checkpoint that dominates it in the Intended BFG.
invalid_example: A supported request-to-operation implementation path reaches the protected operation without any authentication anchor.
exception_policy: Incomplete coverage remains PARTIAL or UNKNOWN and does not prove bypass freedom. Proven bypasses have no implicit exemption.
history: Introduced with coverage-aware Intended BFG dominator enforcement.
